{{Indian name|Mathai|Arakaparampil Mathai}}'''Arakaparampil Mathai "Arak" Mathai''' (28 April 1935 – 20 December 2025)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arak Mathai Obituary - West Hill, ON |url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/west-hill-on/arak-mathai-12675796 |website=Dignity Memorial |language=en-us}}</ref> was an Indian and Canadian [[mathematician]] who has worked in statistics, applied [[analysis]], applications of special functions, and [[astrophysics]]. Mathai established the Centre for Mathematical Sciences, [[Idukki district|Palai]], [[Kerala]], India.

==Education and career==
Mathai was born in Arakulam near Palai in the [[Idukki district]] of [[Kerala]], India as the eldest son of Aley and Arakaparampil Mathai. After completing his high school education in 1953 from St. Thomas High School, Palai, with record marks he joined [[St. Thomas College, Palai]], and obtained his B Sc. degree in mathematics in 1957. In 1959 he completed his master's degree in statistics from [[University of Kerala]], [[Thiruvananthapuram]], Kerala, India, with first class, first rank and gold medal. Then he joined St. Thomas College, Palai, University of Kerala, as a lecturer in Statistics and served there until 1961. He obtained Canadian Commonwealth scholarship in 1961 and went to University of Toronto, Canada, for completing his MA degree in mathematics in 1962. He received his PhD in mathematics from the [[University of Toronto]] in 1964 under the supervision of Ralph Wormleighton.<ref name=mgp>{{Cite web |title=Arakaparampil Mathai - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=15071 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> Mathai then joined [[McGill University]] as an assistant professor and was promoted to an associate professor there in 1968.  He became a full professor at McGill in 1979 and served the department of mathematics and statistics until 2000. From 2000 onwards he was an [[emeritus]] professor of McGill University.

== Honors and awards ==
In 1998, Mathai was awarded the Founder recognition award from the [[Statistical Society of Canada]], which he was heavily involved in its foundation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Founder Recognition Award {{!}} Statistical Society of Canada |url=https://ssc.ca/en/award/founder-recognition-award-0 |website=ssc.ca}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bellhouse |first=David R. |last2=Genest |first2=Christian |date=1999 |title=A History of the Statistical Society of Canada: The Formative Years |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2676647 |journal=Statistical Science |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=80–115 |issn=0883-4237}}</ref> He is a [[fellow]] of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India|National Academy of Sciences]], India<ref>[http://nasi.nic.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=M Fellows], [[National Academy of Sciences, India|National Academy of Sciences]], India. Accessed 24 January 2010</ref> and a fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].<ref>[http://bulletin.imstat.org/pdf/36/3 Centre for Mathematical Sciences, India, receives research grant.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090514153041/http://bulletin.imstat.org/pdf/36/3 |date=14 May 2009 }} IMS  Bulletin, vol. 36, no. 3, April 2007</ref>

==Selected publications==
* Random p-content of a p-parallelotope in Euclidean ''n''-space, ''Advances in Applied Probability'', '''31'''(2), 343&ndash;354 (1999).
* ''An Introduction to Geometrical Probability: Distributional Aspects with Applications'', Gordon and Breach, Newark, (1999).
* ''Jacobians of Matrix Transformations and Functions of Matrix Argument'', [[World Scientific|World Scientific Publishing]], New York, (1997).
* Appell's and Humbert's functions of matrix arguments, ''Linear Algebra and Its Applications'',''' 183''', 202&ndash;221, (1993).
* On non-central generalized Laplacianness of quadratic forms in normal variables, ''Journal of Multivariate Analysis'', '''45''', 239&ndash;246, (1993).
* (With S.B. Provost),	''Quadratic Forms in random Variables: Theory and Applications'', [[Marcel Dekker]], New York, (1992).
* On a system of differential equations connected with the gravitational instability in a multi-component medium in Newtonian cosmology, [[Studies in Applied Mathematics]], '''80''', 75&ndash;93, (1989).
* (With H.J. Haubold), Modern Problems in Nuclear and Neutrino Astrophysics, ''[[Akademie Verlag|Akademie-Verlag]]'', Berlin.
* On a conjecture in geometric probability regarding asymptotic normality of a random simplex, ''Annals of Probability'', '''10''', 247&ndash;251, (1982).
* (With R.S. Katiyar), Exact percentage points for testing independence, [[Biometrika]], '''66''', 353&ndash;356, (1979).
* (With P.N. Rathie), Recent contributions to axiomatic definitions of information and statistical measures through functional equations. In, ''Essays in Probability and Statistics'', Ikeda and others editors, Shinto, Tsusho, Tokyo, pp.&nbsp;607&ndash;633,(1976).
* (With T.A. Davis), Constructing the sunflower head, ''Mathematical Biosciences'',''' 20''', 117&ndash;133, (1974).
